2607.14607.title: Auditing Fairness-Privacy Trade-offs: Subpopulation-Level Effects of Fairness-Enhancing Algorithms
2607.14607.paper_summary: Machine learning (ML) models deployed in sensitive domains such as healthcare, law enforcement, and finance must satisfy not only utility requirements but also fairness and privacy guarantees. While prior work has largely examined how privacy-preserving techniques affect fairness, the inverse question-how fairness-enhancing algorithms influence privacy leakage-remains underexplored. We present the first comprehensive study of how fairness interventions affect membership inference privacy risks at the subpopulation level. By adapting the Likelihood Ratio Attack (LiRA) for subgroup auditing, we uncover privacy disparities that aggregate evaluations obscure. We further analyze how Differential Privacy (DP) interacts with fairness-enhancing methods across different categories, showing that DP's privacy benefits and utility costs are unevenly distributed across subpopulations. Our results demonstrate that fairness interventions do not uniformly increase privacy risk; their impact depends on model architecture, subgroup size, and mitigation strategy. These findings reveal that fairness, privacy, and utility must be jointly evaluated at the subpopulation level, and we introduce the first unified empirical framework to support such auditing in practice.
2607.14607.paper_summary_zh: 機器學習（ML）模型在醫療、執法和金融等敏感領域的部署，必須滿足不僅是效用要求，還包括公平性和隱私保護的保證。雖然先前的研究主要考察了隱私保護技術如何影響公平性，但反向問題——公平性增強算法如何影響隱私洩漏——仍然未被充分探討。我們提出了首個全面研究公平性干預如何影響子群體層級的成員推斷隱私風險的研究。通過調整似然比攻擊（LiRA）以進行子群體審核，我們揭示了聚合評估所掩蓋的隱私差異。我們進一步分析了差分隱私（DP）如何與不同類別的公平性增強方法互動，顯示出DP的隱私效益和效用成本在子群體之間分佈不均。我們的結果表明，公平性干預並不會均勻地增加隱私風險；其影響取決於模型架構、子群體規模和減緩策略。這些發現揭示了公平性、隱私和效用必須在子群體層級共同評估，我們引入了首個統一的實證框架，以支持實踐中的這種審核。
